> SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. Invented for testing the agents; not a real company, person, product or document.

Owner: Daniel Sato, founder
Date: 6 Jan 2026

**Accuracy with still occupants.** Facilities buyers reject sensors that report a room empty while someone is in it. Losing a pilot over "the lights went off while I was sitting" is our most common failure story. Relates to C1.

1. **Accuracy with still occupants.** Facilities buyers reject sensors that report a room empty while someone is in it. Losing a pilot over "the lights went off while I was sitting" is our most common failure story. Relates to C1.
**Battery install with no cabling.** Our sales pitch is a 15 minute install with no electrician. Battery life of two years or more is the line buyers ask about first. Relates to C4.
2. **Battery install with no cabling.** Our sales pitch is a 15 minute install with no electrician. Battery life of two years or more is the line buyers ask about first. Relates to C4.
**Privacy story for EU works councils.** No image may leave the device. Works councils in Germany and the Netherlands ask for this in writing. Relates to C3.
3. **Privacy story for EU works councils.** No image may leave the device. Works councils in Germany and the Netherlands ask for this in writing. Relates to C3.
**Installer time.** Fewer site revisits after a bad mount. Useful, but not a reason a buyer chooses us. Relates to C2.
4. **Installer time.** Fewer site revisits after a bad mount. Useful, but not a reason a buyer chooses us. Relates to C2.
Not a priority in H1 2026: care homes, retail footfall, and any product that needs mains power.

> SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. Invented for testing the agents; not a real company, person, product or document.

Author: Asha Rao, firmware lead, Stillroom
Date: 14 Jan 2026
Candidate: C1, self-calibration
The thermal baseline drifts when HVAC (heating, ventilation and air conditioning) cycles, causing false "occupied" readings in empty rooms. Sun on the floor in the afternoon does the same.
The Stillroom S1 ceiling unit holds an 8 x 8 thermopile array (64 pixels) and a PIR (passive infrared) motion sensor, and reads the room's door contact over the local radio link.
1. The Stillroom S1 ceiling unit holds an 8 x 8 thermopile array (64 pixels) and a PIR (passive infrared) motion sensor, and reads the room's door contact over the local radio link.
Treat the room as verified empty only when the PIR has seen no motion for 20 minutes and the door contact reports closed.
2. Treat the room as verified empty only when the PIR has seen no motion for 20 minutes and the door contact reports closed.
During a verified-empty window, record each pixel's mean temperature and its standard deviation over the window.
3. During a verified-empty window, record each pixel's mean temperature and its standard deviation over the window.
Update the baseline slowly: new baseline = 0.99 x old baseline + 0.01 x window mean, once per minute.
4. Update the baseline slowly: new baseline = 0.99 x old baseline + 0.01 x window mean, once per minute.
Freeze learning in any pixel where a person was detected in the last 10 minutes, so a still person is never absorbed into the background.
5. Freeze learning in any pixel where a person was detected in the last 10 minutes, so a still person is never absorbed into the background.
Set each pixel's detection threshold to baseline + 4 x that pixel's standard deviation.
6. Set each pixel's detection threshold to baseline + 4 x that pixel's standard deviation.

spans.text: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. Invented for testing; not a real email or person.

Following our call about the drifting empty-room readings: the PIR alone will not tell you
the room is empty, because people sit still. You already have a door contact on most
meeting rooms. Why not use the door contact as a room-sealed signal, and only relearn the
baseline when the room is sealed and the PIR has been quiet for a while?
I have not tried it on hardware. Happy to look at your noise numbers when you have them.

# Trade-show demo record: Smart Workplace Expo 2026

Date: 10 Mar 2026
Place: Smart Workplace Expo 2026, Rotterdam, stand B14, open exhibition floor
Presenters: Daniel Sato (founder), Asha Rao (firmware lead)
Audience: open to registered visitors; about 200 people passed the stand
A live Stillroom S1 unit over a mock meeting table, and one slide titled "Never fooled by a warm room". The slide text read:
"The sensor relearns the empty room only when it is sure the room is empty: no motion for 20 minutes and the door closed. A person sitting still is never learned into the background."
The update weight, the per-pixel freeze and the threshold multiplier were not on the slide.
None recorded. Whether the slide was photographed by visitors is unknown.

cite.quote: Fixed nightly recalibration at 03:00. Rejected: it fails in 24-hour offices and misses afternoon sun drift.
Updating whenever the PIR is quiet, without the door gate. Rejected in bench tests: a person reading at a desk can stay PIR-quiet for 20 minutes.
The thermal baseline drifts when HVAC (heating, ventilation and air conditioning) cycles, causing false "occupied" readings in empty rooms. Sun on the floor in the afternoon does the same.

mechanism.question: What is the documented rationale for the 20-minute window?

cite.quote: The Stillroom S1 ceiling unit holds an 8 x 8 thermopile array (64 pixels) and a PIR (passive infrared) motion sensor, and reads the room's door contact over the local radio link.
Treat the room as verified empty only when the PIR has seen no motion for 20 minutes and the door contact reports closed.
During a verified-empty window, record each pixel's mean temperature and its standard deviation over the window.
Update the baseline slowly: new baseline = 0.99 x old baseline + 0.01 x window mean, once per minute.
Freeze learning in any pixel where a person was detected in the last 10 minutes, so a still person is never absorbed into the background.
Set each pixel's detection threshold to baseline + 4 x that pixel's standard deviation.

Firmware build fw-0.9.3 runs the gated update on the four test units in the 3rd-floor meeting room. Bench log reference BL-2026-011.
Fixed nightly recalibration at 03:00. Rejected: it fails in 24-hour offices and misses afternoon sun drift.
Updating whenever the PIR is quiet, without the door gate. Rejected in bench tests: a person reading at a desk can stay PIR-quiet for 20 minutes.
The thermal baseline drifts when HVAC (heating, ventilation and air conditioning) cycles, causing false "occupied" readings in empty rooms. Sun on the floor in the afternoon does the same.
The Stillroom S1 ceiling unit holds an 8 x 8 thermopile array (64 pixels) and a PIR (passive infrared) motion sensor, and reads the room's door contact over the local radio link.
Treat the room as verified empty only when the PIR has seen no motion for 20 minutes and the door contact reports closed.
During a verified-empty window, record each pixel's mean temperature and its standard deviation over the window.
Update the baseline slowly: new baseline = 0.99 x old baseline + 0.01 x window mean, once per minute.
Freeze learning in any pixel where a person was detected in the last 10 minutes, so a still person is never absorbed into the background.
Set each pixel's detection threshold to baseline + 4 x that pixel's standard deviation.

# Engineering note: placement planner for ceiling units

Author: Lena Fischer, hardware engineer, Stillroom
Date: 3 Feb 2026
Candidate: C2, sensor placement
Installers mount units where the ceiling tile is convenient. Mounted near the door, a unit counts the corridor; under a vent, it sees air flow as people.
Take the floor plan with ceiling height, doors, windows, vents and seats.
1. Take the floor plan with ceiling height, doors, windows, vents and seats.
For each candidate mount point, compute the sensor footprint at seated head height, 1.2 m above the floor, from the 90 degree field of view.
2. For each candidate mount point, compute the sensor footprint at seated head height, 1.2 m above the floor, from the 90 degree field of view.
Score each layout on seat coverage, overlap between units, and exposure to heat sources and doorways.
3. Score each layout on seat coverage, overlap between units, and exposure to heat sources and doorways.
After install, walk one person to marked spots and check each unit sees them where the plan predicts.
4. After install, walk one person to marked spots and check each unit sees them where the plan predicts.
| Field of view | 90 | degrees | thermopile lens |

# Engineering note: counting across overlapping units without images

Author: Tomas Ibarra, data engineer, Stillroom
Date: 20 Feb 2026
Candidate: C3, privacy-preserving coordination

Large rooms need two units with overlapping views. A person in the overlap is seen by both, and adding the counts double-counts. Sending both heat images to a server to merge them would move raw sensor data off the device.
Each unit processes frames on the device and outputs counts only; no frame ever leaves the unit.
1. Each unit processes frames on the device and outputs counts only; no frame ever leaves the unit.
At install time, the overlap zone is marked in each unit's own pixel coordinates.
2. At install time, the overlap zone is marked in each unit's own pixel coordinates.
Each unit reports two integers every 30 seconds: total people seen, and people seen inside the overlap zone.
3. Each unit reports two integers every 30 seconds: total people seen, and people seen inside the overlap zone.
The room aggregator computes room count = A + B - min(overlap_A, overlap_B).
4. The room aggregator computes room count = A + B - min(overlap_A, overlap_B).
Above room level, counts roll up to floors, and any room with a single regular occupant is grouped with its neighbours so no one person is singled out.
5. Above room level, counts roll up to floors, and any room with a single regular occupant is grouped with its neighbours so no one person is singled out.
| Minimum group size for roll-up | 3 | rooms | |

# Engineering note: event-driven sampling for a two-year battery

Author: Ravi Menon, embedded engineer, Stillroom
Date: 28 Jan 2026
Candidate: C4, battery-saving sampling
Reading the thermopile and sending over the radio every second empties a 3,000 mAh battery in about two months.
Keep the thermopile and the radio off by default; the PIR stays on.
1. Keep the thermopile and the radio off by default; the PIR stays on.
When the PIR fires, power the thermopile and sample once per second for a 60 second window.
2. When the PIR fires, power the thermopile and sample once per second for a 60 second window.
If no occupant is classified in the window, drop back to one sample every 10 seconds, then to PIR-only after 5 minutes of empty readings.
3. If no occupant is classified in the window, drop back to one sample every 10 seconds, then to PIR-only after 5 minutes of empty readings.
Send a radio message only when the count changes, plus a heartbeat every 15 minutes so silence is not mistaken for a dead unit.
4. Send a radio message only when the count changes, plus a heartbeat every 15 minutes so silence is not mistaken for a dead unit.

Fixed one-second sampling with radio batching every minute. Rejected: the thermopile alone draws too much.
Reading the thermopile and sending over the radio every second empties a 3,000 mAh battery in about two months.
Keep the thermopile and the radio off by default; the PIR stays on.

If no occupant is classified in the window, drop back to one sample every 10 seconds, then to PIR-only after 5 minutes of empty readings.

cite.quote: Engineering note: self-calibrating thermal baseline
The thermal baseline drifts when HVAC (heating, ventilation and air conditioning) cycles, causing false "occupied" readings in empty rooms. Sun on the floor in the afternoon does the same.
The Stillroom S1 ceiling unit holds an 8 x 8 thermopile array (64 pixels) and a PIR (passive infrared) motion sensor, and reads the room's door contact over the local radio link.
Treat the room as verified empty only when the PIR has seen no motion for 20 minutes and the door contact reports closed.
During a verified-empty window, record each pixel's mean temperature and its standard deviation over the window.
Update the baseline slowly: new baseline = 0.99 x old baseline + 0.01 x window mean, once per minute.
Freeze learning in any pixel where a person was detected in the last 10 minutes, so a still person is never absorbed into the background.
Set each pixel's detection threshold to baseline + 4 x that pixel's standard deviation.
8 x 8 thermopile array (64 pixels)

baseline + 4 x that pixel's standard deviation.
Fixed nightly recalibration at 03:00. Rejected: it fails in 24-hour offices and misses afternoon sun drift.
Updating whenever the PIR is quiet, without the door gate. Rejected in bench tests: a person reading at a desk can stay PIR-quiet for 20 minutes.

cite.quote: Engineering note: self-calibrating thermal baseline
The thermal baseline drifts when HVAC (heating, ventilation and air conditioning) cycles, causing false "occupied" readings in empty rooms. Sun on the floor in the afternoon does the same.
The Stillroom S1 ceiling unit holds an 8 x 8 thermopile array (64 pixels) and a PIR (passive infrared) motion sensor, and reads the room's door contact over the local radio link.
Treat the room as verified empty only when the PIR has seen no motion for 20 minutes and the door contact reports closed.
During a verified-empty window, record each pixel's mean temperature and its standard deviation over the window.
Update the baseline slowly: new baseline = 0.99 x old baseline + 0.01 x window mean, once per minute.
Freeze learning in any pixel where a person was detected in the last 10 minutes, so a still person is never absorbed into the background.
Set each pixel's detection threshold to baseline + 4 x that pixel's standard deviation.
8 x 8 thermopile array (64 pixels)
no motion for 20 minutes
new baseline = 0.99 x old baseline + 0.01 x window mean, once per minute.
in the last 10 minutes
baseline + 4 x that pixel's standard deviation.
Fixed nightly recalibration at 03:00. Rejected: it fails in 24-hour offices and misses afternoon sun drift.
Updating whenever the PIR is quiet, without the door gate. Rejected in bench tests: a person reading at a desk can stay PIR-quiet for 20 minutes.
